sections.heading: Vertex Speed Low Shoe
sections.body: Run your climb in this progressive hybrid shoe that combines the specific requirements of climbing into the efficiency of a mountain running shoe. Fly up technical ascents and comfortably back down thanks to a zoned outsole that grips hard rock surfaces and provides traction on soft trail terrain and shock-absorbing underfoot cushion that keeps you feeling stable and lets you feel the ground beneath your feet. The low-profile, stretchy knit collar helps seal out debris.

sections.heading: Konseal Trek Boot
sections.body: The Konseal Trek is built for approaches as demanding as the climb itself—the kind that include scrambling, climbing, and hiking with heavy packs. A responsive underfoot ride and extra lugs around the perimeter provide stability and surefooted grip across uneven terrain, scree, and snow, and the mid-height collar repels debris and adds crucial ankle support for hauling heavy gear to the wall. A multi-height traction pattern on the outsole lets you smear up slabs and descend down softer ground with equal confidence, and the abrasion-resistant upper can withstand harsh alpine conditions for long stretches.

sections.heading: Vertex Alpine GTX Shoe
sections.body: The Vertex Alpine GTX is a complete rethinking of the approach shoe. Balancing the fit and performance of a trail running shoe with the stability required for long days on technical terrain, it’s light, fast, waterproof and combines support and protection with a secure, comfortable ride. A full GORE-TEX liner seals out wet and snow, and the sticky Vibram XS Flash 2 outsole is designed for edging, on-trail performance, and grip in wet and dry conditions. A TPU shank and toe cap add protection, and a knit collar seals out debris. Need a non-waterproof version? Try the Vertex Alpine Shoe .
